channel.title: SqwarkSelf
channel.description: Updates for SqwarkSelf, the Mac focus guard.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
The first SqwarkSelf: a dead-simple focus guard that lives in your menu bar. You say what you're working on, pick how long, and the bird keeps you there.

  • Click the icon, type what you're working on, choose 25, 50 or 90 minutes, press Go. While that watch runs, anything off task goes dark under a veil with a small card — Back to work, or This is work if it really is. Nothing is ever killed or closed.
  • House rules: mark a kind of site or app (Social, Video, Messaging…) as Always, and it is blocked all day. Pause them for 10, 30 or 60 minutes when you need a break.
  • From the keyboard: one shortcut opens a single field wherever you are; type, press Return, and the watch starts.
  • Today shows where the day went. The log stays on your Mac, and a web address is stored without anything after the "?".
  • Optional: Jev, an assistant that is asked only when the rules can't decide. Nothing goes to it from your password manager, banking, Mail or Messages, or from private windows.
  • One licence, US$49 once: up to three Macs and every 1.x update. Paste the key from your email and the bird gets to work. There's no trial — if SqwarkSelf isn't for you, ask for a refund within 14 days, no questions asked.
  • SqwarkSelf can update itself. It asks once whether it may check for updates; you can also press Check for Updates… under Settings → General whenever you like. It never interrupts a watch.
